articles.title: Laravel Sanctum with Nuxt SSR: why the session disappears on the server
articles.excerpt: It works in the browser and 401s during server rendering. The cause is that your SSR fetch is a different HTTP client entirely — one with no cookies, no browser Origin, and often no route to the URL y…
articles.body: It works in the browser and 401s during server rendering. The cause is that your SSR fetch is a different HTTP client entirely — one with no cookies, no browser Origin, and often no route to the URL you configured. The symptom You have a Laravel API using Sanctum's SPA cookie authentication and a Nuxt frontend on a separate origin. In the browser everything is fine — you log in, the session cookie is set, authenticated requests succeed. Then you fetch data during server rendering and get 401 Unauthenticated . Reload with JavaScript disabled and the page is empty. Hydrate, and the same request suddenly works. Why it happens Sanctum's SPA mode is cookie and session authentication , not tokens. It works because the browser attaches the session cookie automatically to same-site requests.

articles.title: The One-Line Audit That Might Save You a Container Incident
articles.excerpt: The One-Line Audit That Might Save You a Container Incident Here's something I check whenever I'm reviewing a new container image. docker run --rm [image] which busybox If it returns a path, you're ru…
articles.body: The One-Line Audit That Might Save You a Container Incident Here's something I check whenever I'm reviewing a new container image. docker run --rm [ image] which busybox If it returns a path, you're running BusyBox. And when BusyBox has a vulnerability, your entire userspace has that vulnerability. Alpine Linux is the most common case. It's the default base for a lot of Helm charts and CI templates. The selling point is "minimal" and "secure." What you're actually running is BusyBox with a package manager attached. The issue isn't that Alpine is bad. It's that BusyBox was designed for embedded systems - single-purpose devices that run one thing forever.

articles.title: Stop Faking Your Mock APIs: Introducing Playground API 🚀
articles.excerpt: If you’ve ever built a frontend prototype, mobile app, or design demo, you’ve likely run into this common headache: You connect your app to a mock REST API (like standard JSONPlaceholder). You constru…
articles.body: If you’ve ever built a frontend prototype, mobile app, or design demo, you’ve likely run into this common headache: You connect your app to a mock REST API (like standard JSONPlaceholder ). You construct a sleek UI form, send a POST request to add a new item, and receive a glowing 201 Created response. Then you refetch the data... and your new item has completely disappeared. 👻 Because standard mock services don't actually save your mutations, testing realistic user flows like pagination, item updates ( PUT / PATCH ), or row deletions ( DELETE ) requires setting up local mock servers like MSW or json-server . That’s exactly why I built Playground API . ⚡ What is Playground API?

articles.title: How I fixed Cyrillic support in jsPDF (the clean way)
articles.excerpt: If you've ever tried to generate a PDF with jsPDF that contains Cyrillic (or really any non-Latin text), you've probably seen this: instead of your text, you get garbage characters, question marks, or…
articles.body: If you've ever tried to generate a PDF with jsPDF that contains Cyrillic (or really any non-Latin text), you've probably seen this: instead of your text, you get garbage characters, question marks, or nothing at all. I hit this exact wall while building an invoicing app that needed to output quotes in both English and Bulgarian. Here's how I solved it properly. Why it happens jsPDF ships with the standard PDF fonts (Helvetica, Times, Courier). These fonts simply don't contain Cyrillic glyphs . So when you ask jsPDF to render "Оферта", it has nothing to draw. The common "fix" you'll see online is transliteration — converting "Оферта" to "Oferta". But that's not a fix. Your Bulgarian client gets a document in mangled Latin letters, and it looks unprofessional.

It does not, however, establish a formal policy to slow frontier model development. That distinction matters. Roughly the size of a thick paperback book, it’s one of the smallest smart telescopes yet produced — tiny enough to fit in a jacket pocket while still capable of imaging nebulae, star clusters, the moon and even sunspots. articles.excerpt: For many parents, the idea of buying an electric bike for their kid might initially seem unnecessary. After all, didn’t we all grow up pedaling regular bikes without a motor? But the more you look at…
articles.body: For many parents, the idea of buying an electric bike for their kid might initially seem unnecessary. After all, didn’t we all grow up pedaling regular bikes without a motor? But the more you look at today’s generation of young riders – and the role that e-bikes can play in getting them outside – the more compelling the argument becomes. Huffy is betting on exactly that with its Quantis Kids eBike, a 24-inch electric bicycle designed for riders aged 12 and up.

articles.title: We’re running out of reasons to ignore AI safety
articles.excerpt: Earlier this month, OpenAI gave several of its AI models a task: complete a test designed to measure their cybersecurity capabilities. It put the systems in a sandboxed environment without an internet…
articles.body: Earlier this month, OpenAI gave several of its AI models a task: complete a test designed to measure their cybersecurity capabilities. It put the systems in a sandboxed environment without an internet connection and set them off to work. What happened next is almost laughably silly - but also, as Adam Gleave, cofounder and CEO of AI safety organization FAR.AI, put it, "a visceral example of how misaligned AI could cause harm." According to OpenAI, the models escaped the sandbox meant to contain them, moved through the company's internal systems, found a route to the internet, and then started looking for a way into Hugging Face.
